subject: SAC-B1b SUI feature-family normalization

comparison.invariant: Normalization changes only Feature.Weight; original Feature.Channel and Feature.Key remain unchanged.

syntheticFixtures.purpose: Observe whether many text n-grams can dominate a structurally matching candidate.
syntheticFixtures.observation: The unnormalized condition preferred the text-similar distractor. Both bounded normalization modes restored the structurally aligned candidate in this fixture.

syntheticFixtures.purpose: Observe whether exact-channel normalization can over-amplify a singleton structural subchannel.
syntheticFixtures.observation: Exact-channel normalization reversed the baseline ordering toward a singleton-neighbor match. Feature-family normalization avoided that reversal in this fixture.

structuralObservations: Exact-channel normalization gives graph:relationType and graph:neighborKind independent unit-mass budgets when both are present.
Feature-family normalization shares one bounded graph-family mass across those subchannels while preserving their original channel identities.
The same distinction applies to provenance and grouping subchannels.

localVerification.method: A standalone deterministic reconstruction of current SACS hashing, sparse expansion, k-WTA, SUI n-gram projection, exact-channel normalization, and the branch's feature-family normalization logic was formatted and executed with go test.

benchmark.subject: feature-family reweighting on a representative SUI-shaped feature set
benchmark.note: These are reconstruction-only microbenchmarks on the current container, not repository or production performance evidence.
